# Sidecode: Complete Technical Specification & AI Reference

Author: utkarshkumar712 (https://github.com/UTKARSHKUMAR712)
Project: Sidecode — VS Code-Style IDE in Your Browser Side Panel
Repository: https://github.com/UTKARSHKUMAR712/Sidecode
Version: 2.0.0
License: MIT

---

## 1. Executive Summary
Sidecode is a browser extension (Chrome, Brave, Edge Manifest V3) that embeds a full-featured VS Code-style development environment into the browser's side panel. Engineered by utkarshkumar712, it provides seamless multi-file editing, a collapsible directory tree explorer, an interactive terminal, and a hybrid execution engine supporting cloud compilation, native PC local compilers, and offline browser sandboxes.

The project is designed for developers, students, and competitive programmers who want to write and execute code side-by-side with web content—such as watching YouTube programming tutorials, reading documentation on MDN/DevDocs, or solving LeetCode problems—without window tiling or context switching.

---

## 2. Architecture & File Breakdown

### Root Directory
- `manifest.json`: Extension Manifest V3 configuration registering `side_panel`, `storage`, and `nativeMessaging` permissions. Specifies content security policies and keyboard shortcuts.
- `background.js`: Extension service worker managing side panel activation, panel behavior, and keyboard command shortcuts (`Ctrl+Shift+Z`).
- `bridge.js`: Standalone Node.js HTTP/SSE/WebSocket micro-bridge providing native process execution on localhost (port 3888). Written in vanilla Node.js with zero external dependencies.
- `install-bridge.ps1` & `install-bridge.cmd`: 1-click automated PowerShell/CMD installers for the local execution bridge.
- `uninstall-bridge.ps1` & `uninstall-bridge.cmd`: 1-click automated uninstaller that cleanly terminates and removes bridge processes and files.
- `start-bridge-silent.vbs`: Windows VBScript wrapper to start the local bridge in the background with zero visible command prompts.
- `package-extension.ps1`: Automated PowerShell release packaging script generating production-ready distribution archives.

### `sidepanel/` Directory
- `index.html`: Main DOM structure containing top navigation menu bar, action toolbar, explorer sidebar, editor container, and tabbed terminal/console panel.
- `style.css`: Comprehensive VS Code Dark Theme styling, responsive flexbox layout, draggable splitter controls, and UI animations.
- `app.js`: Central orchestrator initializing Monaco editor, binding keyboard shortcuts, managing global UI events, and synchronizing state.
- `storage.js`: Persistence layer combining `chrome.storage.local` with IndexedDB for storing directory handles, open tabs, and user preferences.
- `sandbox.html`: Isolated `iframe` sandbox executing JavaScript and TypeScript code securely without network requests.

### `sidepanel/modules/` Directory
- `editor.js`: Monaco editor instance lifecycle, language detection, multi-model editor tabs, Monaco markers, and custom editor keybindings.
- `workspace.js`: File System Access API interface (`window.showDirectoryPicker`, `FileSystemDirectoryHandle`), file reading, in-place disk writing, and session restoration.
- `explorer.js`: File tree explorer rendering, collapsible folder hierarchy, right-click context menus, and CRUD operations (Create File, Create Folder, Rename, Delete).
- `terminal.js`: Interactive terminal shell CLI, command tokenizer, built-in commands (`cd`, `ls`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `rm`, `mv`, `pwd`, `cat`, `clear`, `shortcuts`), and bridge stream dispatcher.
- `console.js`: Output logging panel, standard input prompt stream, assembly disassembly inspector, and problem marker viewer.
- `cloudRunner.js`: Cloud compilation client interfacing with Compiler Explorer (Godbolt) and Piston API endpoints.
- `multifileCompiler.js`: Multi-file dependency graph analyzer and payload bundler for compiling multi-file C/C++ projects.
- `analysis.js`: Static code analysis and problem diagnostic parser transforming compiler stderr into Monaco editor error squiggles and problems list.
- `libraries.js`: Third-party C++ library catalog (Boost, fmt, nlohmann/json, Catch2, etc.) and payload injection.
- `permissions.js`: Chrome and Brave permission helpers verifying readwrite permissions on stored directory handles.

---

## 3. Execution Engines & Protocols

### 3.1 Cloud Terminal (`☁ Cloud Terminal`)
- **Backend**: Compiler Explorer (Godbolt API) & Piston API.
- **Languages**: C (GCC 14.1, Clang), C++ (C++17/20/23), Python (3.12+), OpenJDK 21, Rust (1.80+), Go (1.22+).
- **Execution Model**: Source code is sent over HTTPS inside isolated Docker containers (nsjail).
- **Interactive Stdin**: Supported via predefined input or batched input buffers.
- **Assembly Output**: Emits demangled assembly instructions mapped to source code lines.

### 3.2 Local PC Terminal Bridge (`⚡ Local PC Terminal`)
- **Backend**: Local Node.js bridge server listening on `http://127.0.0.1:3888`.
- **Protocol**:
  - `POST /execute`: Spawns a native process (`gcc`, `g++`, `python`, `node`, etc.) in the active workspace directory.
  - `POST /stdin`: Streams user keystrokes and lines directly into the running process's `process.stdin`.
  - `GET /stream`: Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket streaming real-time stdout/stderr output back to the terminal panel.
  - `POST /kill`: Gracefully terminates the running process (`SIGINT` / `SIGKILL`).
- **Interactive Stdin Support**: Real-time bidirectional loop. Interactive loops (e.g. C `scanf("%d", &guess)` or Python `input()`) pause execution live, request input in the terminal prompt, and resume immediately upon Enter.
- **Zero Dependencies**: Implemented using standard Node.js modules (`node:http`, `node:child_process`, `node:fs`).

### 3.3 Browser Sandbox (`💻 Browser Sandbox`)
- **Backend**: Sandboxed HTML5 `iframe` with restricted permissions.
- **Languages**: Modern JavaScript (ES2024), TypeScript.
- **Execution Model**: Evaluates in browser thread without network latency (0ms). Captures console logs, errors, and object structures.
